items.title: Epic Seven Announces Events for Its Official Steam Launch on October 29
items.summary: Ahead of its official Steam launch on October 29, the mobile RPG Epic Seven has revealed a lineup of events, including a new server called "Foundry" and a Steam demo available from October 8 to October 27.
items.content:
Details of the events planned for the official Steam launch of Epic Seven, a mobile RPG operated by Smilegate and developed by SUPER CREATIVE, were released on October 8 (Thursday). The official Steam service is scheduled to begin on October 29 (Thursday).

On October 29 (Thursday), Epic Seven will begin its official service on Steam, one of the world's largest gaming platforms, and the new server "Foundry" will open at the same time.

A series of events will also be held so that players can get used to the game quickly on the new server.

A settling-in support buff event starting on October 29 (Thursday) offers various effects that support the growth of heroes and accounts, including a 30% increase in EXP gain.

Players who reach account level 70 will receive the hero "Luna," and 20 free summons will also be available every day.

In addition, there will be an event in which players can obtain equipment, growth materials, and hero skins by earning and accumulating points through Arena (PvP) content, along with login bonuses.

The new "Foundry" server can be accessed not only through Steam but also through the PC client "STOVE" and on mobile.

Players can also use their existing account information as is to play on Steam.

From October 8 (Thursday) to October 27 (Tuesday), a demo of Epic Seven can be played on Steam.

The demo is available as part of "2026 Steam Next Fest" and lets players try the main story as well as battle content such as "Brawl," "Battlefield of the War God," and "Automaton Tower."

Progress made in the demo will not carry over to the official service.

The Epic Seven app can be downloaded from Google Play and the App Store. More information about the game is available through the official community and the official YouTube channel.

items.title: Epic Seven E7WC 2026 Group Stage Begins October 10
items.summary: ⓒ SmilegateSmilegate announced that the Group Stage of Epic Seven World Championship 2026 (hereafter E7WC 2026) for Epic Seven (Epic7) will begin on October 10.
items.content:
Korean (한국어) KO Add us on ⓒ Smilegate Smilegate announced that the Group Stage of Epic Seven World Championship 2026 (hereafter E7WC 2026) for Epic Seven (Epic7) will begin on October 10. A total of 28 players who passed the qualifiers will compete over four days.

Now in its sixth edition this year, the tournament features a total prize pool of $100,000. The winner will receive $50,000, and a special skin for a hero chosen by the winner will be produced and added to the game. The finals are scheduled to take place on November 28 at the Lotte Cinema World Tower Super Plex in Jamsil.

The Group Stage schedule spans October 10 and 11, as well as October 17 and 18. Participating players are divided into groups of four to compete in a double-elimination format. The top two players from each group will advance to the Knockout Stage. Epic Seven Masters 2026 winner Hazamarei and runner-up MagicQi advance directly to the Knockout Stage, where they will compete against the players advancing from the Group Stage for the title of World Champion.

Developed by Super Creative, Epic Seven is a mobile turn-based strategic RPG featuring real-time PvP (player vs. player) content called "World Arena". E7WC 2026 is a tournament to determine the world's best player in this content, featuring players from the "Global," "Europe," "Korea," "Japan," and "Asia" servers.

All matches from the Group Stage to the finals will be broadcast live in four languages on ChZZk and Twitch. Smilegate plans to host Drops events for viewers and reveal coupon codes during live broadcasts. In-game, a match prediction event will be held where players can earn rewards by predicting match results.

With an update on October 8, Epic Seven is also adding "Mei Lin," a collaboration Hero with the IP Chaos Zero Nightmare (hereafter CZN). "Mei Lin" is the third collaboration Hero introduced following "Haru" and "Renoa".

Detailed information regarding the game can be found on the official Epic Seven community and official YouTube channel.

items.title: Epic Seven Officially Launches on Steam Oct. 29, Opens New Server
items.summary: © SmilegateSmilegate will launch the official Steam service for its mobile turn-based strategy RPG Epic Seven on October 29.
items.content:
Korean (한국어) KO Add us on © Smilegate Smilegate will launch the official Steam service for its mobile turn-based strategy RPG Epic Seven on October 29. Along with opening a new server, the company will hold growth support events and release a Steam demo ahead of the official launch.

On October 8, Smilegate announced the Steam release schedule and key event details for Epic Seven, developed by Super Creative. The new server, "Foundry," added alongside the official service launch, can be accessed not only through Steam but also via the STOVE PC client and mobile devices. Players can also play the game on Steam while retaining their existing account data.

Growth support events for new server players will begin on October 29. The "Settlement Support Buff Event" provides hero and account growth benefits, including a 30% boost to EXP earned. Players who reach Account Level 70 will receive the hero "Luna," and 20 free daily summons will also be provided.

Additionally, an event will reward players with equipment, growth materials, and hero skins based on their cumulative points earned in the PvP mode "Arena." Separate login rewards will also be provided for players.

Ahead of the official service, an Epic Seven demo will be available on Steam from 6:00 PM on October 8 until October 27. Released as part of "2026 Steam Next Fest," the demo allows players to experience main story content alongside major battle modes such as "Brawl," "Battlefield of the War God," and "Automaton Tower". However, gameplay progress made in the demo will not carry over to the official service.

Further details regarding Epic Seven's official Steam service and events can be found on the official community and YouTube channel.

items.title: Epic Seven Joins Steam Next Fest With a Playable Demo
items.summary: Epic Seven, the mobile RPG operated by Smilegate Megaport, is joining Steam Next Fest, running from October 19 to 26, with a playable demo available on Steam from October 8 to October 26 ahead of the game
items.content:
Epic Seven, the mobile RPG developed by SUPER CREATIVE and operated by Smilegate Megaport, is joining "Steam Next Fest," running from October 19 (Monday) to October 26 (Monday). The announcement was made on September 17 (Thursday).

Ahead of the event, a playable demo of Epic Seven will be available on Steam from October 8 (Thursday) through October 26 (Monday), giving players a chance to try the game before its official Steam launch later this year.

Steam Next Fest is an event where players can try free demos of numerous upcoming Steam titles for about a week at a time. It is held three times a year, in February, June, and October.

The Epic Seven demo lets players experience the main story along with battle content such as "Brawl," "Battlefield of the War God," and "Automaton Tower."

The demo also opens up arena content where players can battle one another, including both the Normal Arena and the Rookie Arena.

During the event, Smilegate Megaport will provide Skystones, summoning items, and various growth materials so players can fully enjoy the content, with powerful gear sets also being distributed in the latter half of the period.

Epic Seven is also planning to officially launch on Steam by the end of this year.

Through account linking with Steam, players will be able to carry over their existing account data and continue playing on Steam without losing progress.

In addition, for players trying Epic Seven for the first time on Steam, a new region will be opened for a set period, running on an independent matchmaking server, and controller support will also be added, offering a new way to play.

The Steam store page opened on August 22, and a wishlist registration event is currently underway.

Epic Seven can be downloaded from Google Play and the App Store. More information about the game is available through the official community and the official YouTube channel.

items.content:
Korean (한국어) KO Add us on ⓒ Smilegate Smilegate announced on the 17th that Epic Seven, the mobile turn-based strategy RPG developed by Super Creative, will participate in Steam Next Fest 2026, held from October 19 to 26 Pacific Standard Time (PST).

Steam Next Fest is an event where players can try free demos of upcoming games on Steam for one week. It is held three times a year in February, June, and October.

The Epic Seven demo will open ahead of the event, running from October 8 to 26. In the demo, players can experience combat content including the main story, Brawl, Battlefield of the War God, and Automaton Tower. PvP modes such as Normal Arena and Rookie Arena will also be accessible.

During the event period, Smilegate plans to provide Skystones, summoning currency, and growth materials needed for testing, as well as equipment sets in the latter half of the event.

Epic Seven is scheduled to officially launch on Steam within 2026. Players will be able to play with their existing accounts by linking them to Steam, and the game will also introduce a new region featuring an independent matchmaking server for new users, alongside controller support. The Steam store page opened on August 22, and a wishlist event is currently underway.

items.title: Epic Seven Pity Odds: 1.5% Rate, $302 Guarantee [2026]
items.summary: Epic Seven's 1.5% base rate has no 50/50 — 121 pulls guarantees your hero for 02-18. See the full cost table and EV math.
items.content:
Epic Seven’s gacha has one feature that sets it apart from almost every other anime-style gacha on the market: there is no 50/50 coin flip. The short answer for anyone deciding whether to chase a specific hero is this – Smilegate sets the base rate for a 5-star hero at 1.5% per pull on a Covenant pickup banner, and backs that up with a hard, deterministic guarantee at 121 pulls that hands you the exact featured hero, not a random 5-star from the wider pool. Priced out in real money, that guarantee runs roughly $302 to $318 depending on how you buy your Skystones, based on Epic Seven’s own currency shop and current App Store pricing.

How Epic Seven’s Summon System Works The Base 5-Star Rate: What 1.5% Really Means Epic Seven’s Biggest Difference: No 50/50 Coin Flip The 121-Pull Hard Pity, Explained Pull-by-Pull Probability Table What It Costs: Skystones, Bookmarks, and the Math Between Them The Pity-Cost Table: Currency and Real Cash at Every Milestone Step-by-Step Expected Value Calculation Five Worked Examples: What Different Budgets Actually Buy How Epic Seven Compares to Other Gacha Pity Systems Myths vs. Facts About Epic Seven’s Gacha Is Chasing a Specific Hero in Epic Seven Worth It? Frequently Asked Questions What is Epic Seven’s base rate for a 5-star hero? Does Epic Seven have a 50/50 system? How many pulls does it take to guarantee a featured hero? How much does it cost to guarantee a hero in Epic Seven? Is it cheaper to buy Skystones in bulk? When does soft pity start in Epic Seven? Is Epic Seven’s rate disclosure considered reliable? Should I save Skystones for a specific banner, or spend as I go? Related Coverage That’s the headline. The rest of this piece walks through where those numbers come from, what a pull-by-pull probability curve looks like under the published 1.5% base rate, a step-by-step expected-value calculation, a worked pity-cost table priced in both Skystones and dollars, and five spending scenarios so you can judge whether saving up for one hero is worth it before you open your wallet.

Epic Seven runs its gacha through “Covenant Summons,” which pull from a shared pool of heroes and artifacts. A single summon costs 5 Covenant Bookmarks, and Bookmarks are bought with Skystones, the game’s premium currency, according to BlueStacks’ Epic Seven beginner’s guide . The in-game shop sells 5 Bookmarks for 100 Skystones at the standard rate, or 50 Bookmarks for 950 Skystones as a bulk option, which works out to 95 Skystones per summon instead of 100, per Epic7DB’s currency guide .

The banner that matters most for anyone chasing a specific hero is the Covenant “Drop Rate Up” banner, sometimes called a pickup banner, which rotates roughly every one to two weeks and features a single highlighted 5-star hero. As of early September 2026, that rotation included heroes like Uncharted Pioneer Politis on a Drop Rate Up banner starting September 3, and Lisette on a Mystic pull banner from late August, according to the Epic Seven Wiki’s heroes hub , confirming the game is still actively live-serviced with fresh banners rather than winding down.

Every Covenant pickup summon draws from a rarity table where the top tier, 5-star heroes, sits at a flat base rate of roughly 1.5% before any pity boost kicks in, according to a September 2026 update to the Epic Seven Wiki’s summons and pity guide . That rate has crept upward over the game’s history. Older third-party breakdowns from 2019 and 2020 cited figures closer to 1.25% to 1.4% for a 5-star hero, so the current 1.5% figure reflects a modest rate increase Smilegate has made to the base odds over time, not a number that’s stayed frozen since launch.

What makes that 1.5% figure different from base rates in most other gacha games is what happens after it hits. In games like Genshin Impact or Honkai: Star Rail, a 5-star pull is often followed by a second roll of the dice over which specific unit you actually receive. Epic Seven skips that step entirely on pickup banners, which is the single biggest reason its pity math is simpler to calculate than almost anything else in the genre.

Most modern gacha systems layer a 50/50 mechanic on top of their pity count: hit the top rarity, and there’s roughly a coin-flip chance it’s the character the banner is actually selling rather than a generic unit from the standard pool. Epic Seven doesn’t do that on its Covenant pickup banners. The Epic Seven Wiki states it plainly: “Covenant pickup pity is 121 pulls and there is no 50/50,” and that if the banner has a featured hero up, “the 121st yellow is that hero.”

That single design choice changes the entire cost calculation compared to a game like Genshin Impact’s 50/50 pity system , where losing the coin flip can force a second full pity cycle before you’re guaranteed the unit you actually wanted. In Epic Seven, once you’ve committed to a pickup banner, every pull that doesn’t land a 5-star still counts toward the same 121-pull counter, and there’s no branch where you land the top rarity and still walk away without the hero you were saving for.

Epic Seven layers a soft pity ramp on top of the flat base rate starting around pull 100, and that ramp climbs until it reaches a deterministic guarantee at pull 121, per the Epic Seven Wiki’s summons documentation. Put simply: if you haven’t landed the featured hero by your 120th pull on a given pickup banner, your 121st summon is that hero, full stop, no roll involved.

Smilegate hasn’t published the exact per-pull rate curve for the 21 pulls between where soft pity starts and where hard pity locks in, so this article doesn’t estimate specific percentages for that stretch. What’s confirmed is the start point (around pull 100), the endpoint (pull 121, guaranteed), and that the climb in between only raises your odds, never lowers them. That’s enough to build a conservative, fully sourced cost model without guessing at numbers nobody has published.

Using the flat 1.5% base rate that applies through pull 99 (before soft pity begins), the cumulative chance of landing the featured hero at least once follows the standard formula for repeated independent draws: 1 minus (0.985 raised to the power of the pull count). Here’s how that curve looks at common milestones.

Read that table as a floor, not a ceiling. Every percentage above pull 99 is understated, because it doesn’t credit the rising soft-pity odds that a real player benefits from between pulls 100 and 120. The only number in that range you can bank on with certainty is the last one: 121 pulls always closes the gap.

Translating pulls into dollars takes two conversions: Skystones to Bookmarks, and Skystones to USD. The first part is fixed by the shop. Buying Bookmarks 5 at a time costs 100 Skystones per summon; buying them 50 at a time (the bundle tied to a 10-pull) costs 950 Skystones, or 95 Skystones per summon, a roughly 5% discount for buying in bulk, according to Epic Seven’s Skystone farming guide .

The second conversion, Skystones to real money, comes from Epic Seven’s own storefront. Player-reported regional pricing and third-party top-up listings both point to the same top-tier denomination: 3,800 Skystones for $99.99, the largest single Skystone-only package currently sold, based on pricing mirrored on Epic Seven’s official top-up denominations listed via LootBar and cross-checked against Epic Seven’s own Apple App Store listing , which shows a $99.99 top tier among its in-app purchases. That works out to roughly 2.63 cents per Skystone at the top denomination, the cheapest per-unit rate in the shop.

items.title: Epic Seven's 8th Anniversary Update: Everything Revealed
items.summary: Epic Seven's 8th anniversary showcase revealed a new episode, a roguelike mode, a Chaos Zero Nightmare collab, a Steam launch, and much more.
items.content:
Gaming Epic Seven's 8th Anniversary Update: Everything Revealed GameDaily Follow Franz Christian Irorita Mon, August 24, 2026 at 7:30 PM UTC Epic Seven 's 8th Anniversary Infinity Showcase brought a genuinely large wave of announcements, from a new story episode and heroes to a Steam launch and a major crossover collaboration. Here's everything that has been revealed.

The anniversary showcase revealed a new Side Episode, Paradise Lost, set in the 1st World, the earliest setting in the Epic Seven universe.

Two new heroes join alongside it: Lisette, the alter ego of Goddess Diche, a Light-elemental Soul Weaver built around reviving and restoring allies, and Uncharted Pioneer Politis, introduced at the moment of her first landing on Orbis in the 1st World, whose role shifts depending on where she's placed on the team.

Acolyte of the End Kayron will factor heavily into Paradise Lost's story and gets a separate, dedicated introduction later, while a character named Kain will appear as a playable NPC rather than a summonable hero.

Background Battling now keeps running even after the game is closed, with players able to register up to 100 Leif, roughly 400 runs, and duration now calculated against a player's actual clear records rather than a flat estimate. New auto-sell and auto-extract options for Equipment are coming alongside it.

An Equipment Charm Payback Event starts August 27 and runs three weeks, returning a set percentage of invested EXP as Greater Charm Selection Chests. Ogre's Armory is being folded into the Hunt menu as new content called Ogre Hunt, available at Otherworld Difficulty and offering Reversal, Riposte, Warfare, and Pursuit Sets.

Rift is being temporarily suspended starting August 27 for content restructuring. Profile Cards are also getting a refresh, with layers increasing from 100 to 130, saved slots doubling from 5 to 10, and new colors, shapes, emoji placement, direct coordinate input, PC shortcuts, and a gift-to-friend option added.

A new World Arena mode called The Call of Chaos brings 3v3 arcade-style PvP with a fast pick-ban phase, roughly a minute long with up to three rerolls, followed immediately by combat.

The goal is to destroy the opponent's Sentinel, with players able to trigger various ally buffs or enemy debuffs by choosing a "Fate" mid-battle. Runs end at 7 wins or 3 losses, with better rewards for more wins, and players earn Ranking Points and shop currency along the way, with season-based ranking rewards on top.

Super Creative is bringing its other major title into Epic Seven this September, crossing over with Chaos Zero Nightmare .

Renoa arrives as a free character during the collaboration period, while Haru and Mei Lin will be available through Limited Summon. Several collaboration events, including a Counseling Center and dedicated shop, will run in Witchaven for the duration.

It's a natural pairing for Super Creative, which has been actively cross-promoting CZN alongside its other titles at events like Anime Expo 2026 as the newer, darker-toned game builds its own audience.

Epic Seven 's first official roguelike mode, Dimensional Exploration, launches with unlimited attempts and no entry currency required.

Players form a 3-Hero team, choose special effects through Expedition Supplies, and can assign up to three additional heroes to tag slots to swap in mid-battle, for up to seven usable heroes total.

items.title: 'Chaos Zero Nightmare' Collaboration Kicks Off in September; 'Epic Seven' Unveils 8th Anniversary Showcase
items.summary: ©Super CreativeSuper Creative released the INFINITY Showcase video today (Aug. 22) to celebrate the 8th anniversary of its hero collector RPG, 'Epic Seven'.
items.content:
Offline mode support, Steam release, and new content teased

Korean (한국어) KO Add us on ©Super Creative Super Creative released the INFINITY Showcase video today (Aug. 22) to celebrate the 8th anniversary of its hero collector RPG, 'Epic Seven'. In this showcase, Producer Tak Kwang-jin and Development Director Heo Dae-kyun appeared to announce key details, including the 8th anniversary update, online and offline events, and the roadmap ahead.

Side story episode 'Paradise Lost' unveiled, covering the very first Era

For this 8th anniversary, Epic Seven will delve into the 1st Era, the earliest period in its lore. Previously, Epic Seven mainly portrayed the story of the protagonist Ras fulfilling his mission as the Heir of the Covenant in the Seventh World, and subsequently becoming human to travel across the realm, overcoming crises alongside new companions. Since then, starting with the 6th Era episode in 2025 and the 5th Era side story episode 'Rain of Fading Embers', the game expanded its universe by showcasing settings and characters from previous eras. Now, with the 8th anniversary, Epic Seven aims to firmly establish its lore based on its origin story.

The 1st Era takes place before Ras existed, centering around Kayron as a human before becoming an Apostle, Politis who came to Orbis while investigating the truth behind the destruction of her homeworld, and Lizette, the manifestation of Goddess Diche. The central hero, Lizette, is a Light-element Soul Weaver who sacrificed everything to protect Orbis. Reflecting this concept, she possesses a passive skill that revives allies as Shards of Life. Allied heroes in the Shard of Life state take no damage and return to their original hero form after 2 turns to rejoin the battle. Her Skill 3, 'Convergent Time', restores the Health of all allies and increases Speed for 3 turns. If she is in the Divinity state, she triggers 'Time Rewind' for all allies except herself, resetting them to the state they were in at the start of battle.

Another major hero, 'Unknown Pioneer Politis', showcases a unique gimmick fitting her pioneer concept, where her assigned role changes based on her placement. When placed in the front row, she receives an offensive role, and when in the back row, she receives a defensive role, altering her skill effects accordingly—making strategic placement based on team composition a key point. Additionally, Kayron before becoming an Apostle, named 'Cain', will appear as an NPC rather than a new summonable hero, while Apostle of the End Kayron will be introduced separately at a later date.

Offline mode support, quality-of-life improvements, and content overhauls announced

Following the introduction of the Paradise Lost story, details regarding quality-of-life improvement patches were unveiled. First, offline mode support will be added to Battle Delegation. Previously, playing Epic Seven required keeping auto-battle running continuously to farm Hunts, but going forward, Battle Delegation will operate offline based on actual clear records. Players can queue up to 100 Leifs (Stamina currency), and automatic equipment sale and extraction features will also apply. Alongside these improvements, an Equipment Charm Payback event will run for three weeks starting August 27 to reduce players' equipment enhancement burden. During this period, players can receive refunds in Greater Universal Equipment Charm Selection Chests proportional to the EXP spent on equipment enhancement.

Additionally, 'Ogre's Armory', which previously served as early-game equipment farming content, has seen lower utility due to revamped early progression systems. As a result, it will be integrated into the Hunt menu as the new 'Ogre Hunt'. In Ogre Hunt, players will be able to obtain the Revenge, Counter, Opening, and Pursuit sets, which were previously obtainable only in Rift. Meanwhile, 'Rift'—which was initially added to capture the feel of massive boss battles—has become repetitive farming content and overlaps with other modes, so it will be temporarily removed and re-released after an overhaul.

In addition to PvE combat content, customization elements will be expanded. Profile Cards will see their max layers increased to 130 and available slots expanded to 10. New colors, shapes, and emotes will also be added, along with a feature allowing players to position elements by directly entering coordinates. PC hotkeys will also be supported, and a friend gifting feature will be added.

Meanwhile, a new PvP mode named 'Call of Chaos' will be added. Call of Chaos is a new mode in World Arena, designed as a 3v3 arcade-style PvP where players can jump straight into the fun of battle. The pick/ban phase lasts about one minute and drops the sequential pick/ban system in favor of displaying random heroes all at once for battle. Players can reroll heroes they wish to swap up to two times to build their team.

The win condition also differs. While traditional World Arena requires defeating all enemy heroes to win, Call of Chaos awards victory to the side that destroys the enemy's rear-row Guardian first. As long as the Guardian is alive, it continuously revives fallen heroes, offering a thrill of dynamic comebacks distinct from standard battles. Additionally, the roguelike element 'Destiny' will appear during battle, allowing players to buff allies or debuff enemies to turn the tide. A Call of Chaos run ends upon reaching 7 wins or 3 losses; rewards increase with each victory, and completing a run awards ranking points and shop currency. Season ranks will be tallied based on ranking points, granting additional rank rewards.

Chaos Zero Nightmare collaboration kicks off in September; permanent roguelike mode 'Dimension Exploration' added

Additionally, a collaboration with Super Creative's other anime collector RPG, 'Chaos Zero Nightmare', has been confirmed for September. The story will follow Renoa, Haru, and Meyrin after they crash-land into the world of Epic Seven due to a sudden Chaos Gate opening aboard the SS Nightmare. Among them, Renoa, who appears as a Moonlight hero, can be obtained for free during the event period, while Haru and Meyrin will be available through limited summons.

items.title: Epic Seven Unveils Summer Hero Orb Update
‘Epic Seven’ “Secret Summer” Update Live—New Limited Hero, Story, “Epic Dash” Event
items.summary: This week, developer Super Creative and publisher Smilegate have launched their latest summer update to their free-to-play turn-based role-playing game
items.content:
This week, developer Super Creative and publisher Smilegate have launched their latest summer update to their free-to-play turn-based role-playing game title ‘Epic Seven’ across PC and mobile platforms. This seasonal update includes a new Limited Hero, a Special Side Story, and the latest “Epic Dash” event. A special summer coupon code, “E7SUMMERGIFT26”, is also available for redemption until 26 August—you can redeem it in-game or by clicking over here .

The Limited Hero introduced for the 2026 summer season is Eye of the Abyss Fumyr. As a central figure in the newly added Special Side Story, “Show Me What Lies Within,” she visits the Aelo Coast to track the whereabouts of Harsetti, the sovran of Shadow Elves, only to find herself swept up in a series of unexpected incidents.

Eye of the Abyss Fumyr is a 5★ Earth Elemental Mage obtainable until July 16. Her Skill 3, “Eye of the Abyss,” inflicts “Detain” on the foremost enemy Hero, temporarily removing them from the battlefield. This allows players to collapse the enemy’s frontline and drive the battle to their advantage.

Story starring Fumyr will run for six weeks until 6 August. Set against a coastal backdrop, the narrative features a diverse cast of characters alongside Fumyr, including the information broker “Birgitta” and her assistant “Aube.” Notably, as players progress through the story, they can play a classic “territory-capture” style arcade mini game to acquire various rewards, including high-quality illustrations.

Meanwhile, the “Epic Dash” event will take place from June 25 to August 27, offering massive benefits for Hero acquisition and growth. Players can clear daily and weekly missions to level up their “Mission Pass” rank and claim rewards. Depending on their rank, players can obtain a 5★ Hero Selector that provides a Hero with all progression fully completed, a 5★ Limited Hero Selector, a standard 5★ Hero Selector, various Summon Currencies, Equipment Sets, and more.

Also, as part of the Epic Dash lineup, the “Premium Moonlight Summon” event will grant players up to 100 free Moonlight Hero summons simply by logging in daily. As an extra milestone bonus, players will receive a 5★ Light Elemental Hero Summon Ticket upon performing 20 summons, and a 5★ Dark Elemental Hero Summon Ticket upon performing 100 summons. Finally, the update brings the “Lucky Dash” event, where players can obtain various Equipment and Charms, alongside the “Epic Dash Buff” event, which provides several powerful in-game buffs.

The developer has also prepared a set of “Secret Summer Digital Merchandise” featuring wallpapers of some of Epic Seven’s heroines. You can download the images from the game’s official website (bottom of the page) to grab copies tailor-made for your PC, mobile, tablet, and watch.

Epic Seven is available as a free-to-play title across PC via STOVE , iOS , and Android via Google Play .
